=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py:421-424 (also 525-526 per minimax_minimax-m3) | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In `_gate_dispatch_steps`, the cap regex `^          DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS: "([0-9]+)"$` matches only a quoted integer. An unquoted value, an Actions expression such as `${{ vars.X }}`, or a job-level `env:` entry gives cap_match=None, and the step is silently scored as the 1500 default.
  WHY: The floor test and the step-budget test still pass while the workflow could run with a cap below the floor, so a regression like the 2026-11-27 refusal could get past the guard issue #10205 item 4 asks for. All reviewers rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
- README.md:379 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The rewritten `DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS` Default column says "every dispatch step in `test-and-mark-stable.yml` sets `1500`". The "Dispatch & snapshot — workflow-log-analysis" step (.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:3726-3781, env 3742-3749) sets no such entry and relies on the script default.
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime because the effective cap is 1500 either way. The README now contradicts the workflow and agents.d/10205-gate-dispatch-rate-limit-cap-floor.md, which says "the workflow-log-analysis snapshot relies on the default". All reviewers rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4245-4247 (also 4312-4316 per z-ai_glm-5_3-flash; tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py:487-490 per openai_gpt-6-luna) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The 81-minute `orchestrate-decompose-test` budget (3000s watch + 1500s cap + 360s other steps = 4860s) leaves out the 64s dispatch margin (4s pre-sleep + 60s). The worst-case dispatch of 4564s leaves only 296s for the other steps, not the 360s the comment states.
  WHY: Reviewers disagree on severity, and the highest is used. openai_gpt-6-luna rated it MAJOR: the job can be cancelled before the other steps finish, and it needs at least 82 minutes. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rated it NIT and deliberately downgraded the pass-1 MAJOR because no evidence shows an overrun; it treats the defect as inaccurate comment arithmetic (fix: 82 min or restate 296s). minimax_minimax-m3 rated it NIT as pre-existing drift the PR carried forward. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 checked it and chose not to report it, saying 3000+1500+360=4860 is correct and 4564s fits.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

(No task gaps reported.)

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py:_gate_dispatch_steps(), lines `cap_match = re.search(r'^          DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS: "([0-9]+)"$', header, re.M)` and `cap = int(cap_match.group(1)) if cap_match else 1500` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test only recognises a quoted-integer cap. An unquoted value, an expression, or a job-level `env:` entry (job_header is never searched) is scored as the 1500 default.
  WHY: The floor test and the step-budget check pass while the script runs with a lower cap and prints outcome=cap_reached on a refusal like the 505s one. A one-character YAML change gets past the guard issue #10205 item 4 asks for. Hardening suggestion: assert cap_match is not None when the variable appears in the header, and check job_header too (HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1).
- README.md:`DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS` row, Default column | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The "Dispatch & snapshot — workflow-log-analysis" step (.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:3726-3781, env block at 3742-3749) does not set the variable; only five of the six dispatch steps set it explicitly.
  WHY: Nothing fails, but the README disagrees with the workflow and with agents.d/10205-gate-dispatch-rate-limit-cap-floor.md.
- Note: the reviewer checked the pass-1 MAJOR at .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4245-4247 and chose not to report it, saying the arithmetic is correct and 4564s fits within 4860s. It reported no task gaps and did not measure the 480,000-byte workflow size because no shell was available.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- README.md:379 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The documentation wrongly states that every dispatch step in test-and-mark-stable.yml explicitly sets DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS to 1500.
  WHY: The "Dispatch & snapshot — workflow-log-analysis" step relies on the script default. This is a documentation-accuracy issue.
- tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py:421-424 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The regex r'^          DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS: "([0-9]+)"$' only matches quoted integer strings.
  WHY: An unquoted integer falls back to the 1500 default, which could hide a value below the 1500s floor.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- README.md:line 379, the `DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS` row Default column | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The claim that every dispatch step "sets `1500`" is inaccurate. The `Dispatch & snapshot — workflow-log-analysis` step (.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml around line 3726-3749) has no entry, and the README contradicts `agents.d/10205-gate-dispatch-rate-limit-cap-floor.md:2`.
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime. This is documentation drift introduced by the README rewrite.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:lines 4245-4247 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The comment's 3000 + 1500 + 360 = 4860 math ignores the 64s dispatch margin the contract test reserves (tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py:428-431), so the real budget for the other steps is 296s, not 360s.
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime. The comment overstates the slack by 64s, and the same drift was already there before the PR, which carried it forward rather than introducing it.
- tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py:lines 421-424 (`_gate_dispatch_steps`) and lines 525-526 (`test_update_workflows_step_cap_replays_2026_11_27_refusal`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The regex requires a quoted integer literal; an unquoted value or an expression falls through to the 1500 default.
  WHY: This is a defensive gap, not a current failure: a future `${{ vars.CAP }}` that resolves below the floor would get past the test.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4245-4247; tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py:487-490 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The 81-minute job budget assumes 360s for the other steps, but the contract test checks only the dispatch budget plus the 64s margin and does not also reserve those 360s.
  WHY: 4,564s of dispatch plus margin leaves 296s of the 4,860s limit, so the job can be cancelled before the other steps finish. It needs at least 82 minutes.
- tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py:421-423 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A cap value that is present but not a quoted integer is treated as absent and assumed to be 1,500s.
  WHY: An unquoted `410` or an expression below the floor would still pass the test.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4245-4247 (job comment + timeout-minutes: 81) and 4312-4316 (orchestrate dispatch env comment) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The orchestrate budget comment leaves out the 4s pre-sleep and 60s margin, so the worst case is 1500 + 3000 + 64 = 4564s, leaving 296s rather than 360s. This misses issue #10205 deliverable 3, which requires accurate arithmetic in the budget comments.
  WHY: The job could be cancelled mid-cleanup if the other steps exceed about 292s. Fix: timeout-minutes: 82, or restate 296s. The reviewer deliberately downgraded the pass-1 MAJOR because no runtime artifact shows an overrun.
- README.md:line 379, `DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS` row, Default column | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The README says "every dispatch step in `test-and-mark-stable.yml` sets `1500`", but the workflow-log-analysis step (test-and-mark-stable.yml:3726) has no entry, which contradicts agents.d/10205-gate-dispatch-rate-limit-cap-floor.md.
  WHY: Nothing fails, but the documentation is inaccurate on a line this PR rewrote.
- tests/test_dispatch_and_watch_rate_limit.py:421-424 (`_gate_dispatch_steps`, cap_match regex `DISPATCH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS: "([0-9]+)"`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A non-literal value (e.g. `${{ vars.SOME_CAP }}` resolving to "410") gives cap_match=None and is assumed to be 1500. The existing `test_gate_dispatch_steps_fit_rate_limit_cap_in_step_budget` uses the same parser and has the same gap.
  WHY: The test can silently stop enforcing the floor after a future edit. Hardening suggestion: assert cap_match is not None when the variable is in the header (HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2).
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
